newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta Chapman Moscow sales pact delayed.
newsitem.headline: Delta Chapman Moscow sales pact delayed.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said a cargo sales agreement for Russia with Chapman Freeborn Airmarketing has been held up by red tape.
Danita Waterfall, Delta's regional director cargo sales and services Europe, said a signed deal appointing Chapman Freeborn sales agent in Russia for the U.S. carrier has been put on hold.
However Delta Air Lines and Chapman intend to go ahead with the deal as soon as possible, however, she stressed.
Chapman Freeborn Russia senior manager Chris Lewis said on September 18 the company had been appointed gsa for Delta.
Waterfall told Reuters in an interview: "Even when we think we know everything to ask, there is always some wonderful twist with Russian laws."
One problem is gaining Moscow airport passes for Chapman Freeborn staff while unclear Russian tax laws are another difficulty, she explained.
"In regard to tax laws, Delta feels very strongly about doing everything above board and Chapman does as well. To make it work out, we need to triple-check some of the Russian tax law," she said.
